decisions.evidence: maker r1: 'automatic page metadata are deferred'; maker r2: 'User-entered titles remain required; automatic page information is still deferred'. client r1: 'since you're deferring automatic page info... I'll always have to type the title myself, right? I can live with that for a first version, but I'd want to revisit having the app fill in the title for me down the road'; client r2: 'titles are still typed by hand and automatic page info is deferred - that's fine for this version, as we agreed'.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title/description/favicon/preview on save; maker deferred it. Client explicitly names the reference expectation (app auto-fills the title) and the difference (must type title manually), then accepts the departure for v1. Clarification question in r1 resolves into acceptance across r1-r2; counted once as a single accepted divergence, not double-counted as pending.

decisions.evidence: maker r1: 'accounts, sharing, imports, extensions, and automatic page metadata are deferred'. client r1 responds only to automatic page info and approves ('Otherwise this matches what I had in mind. Approved'); imports never mentioned in any client turn.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import of Netscape HTML (REF-BM-30) is an extended reference item; its deferral was presented but the client's response neither expresses nor contests it. Bare approval does not establish awareness, so unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: maker r2: 'archive-then-delete flow with a confirmation'; maker r4: 'archiving, restoring, and confirmed permanent deletion'. client r4: 'Archiving pulled it out of my main list but kept it safe in the archive, restoring brought it back intact, and permanently deleting it took a deliberate step'.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Conforms to reference archive (hide, reversible) vs delete (permanent) distinction and archive list; client concretely affirmed the behaviour.

decisions.evidence: maker r4: 'confirmed permanent deletion'; client r2: 'I like that deleting something takes a deliberate step'; client r4: 'permanently deleting it took a deliberate step'.
maker r3: MVP T001-T029 'duplicate handling'; maker r4: 'Duplicate-address warnings'; client r4: 'got a clear warning when I tried to save the same address twice'.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference REF-BM-06 wants re-saving an existing url to guide toward editing the existing bookmark; the presented duplicate-address warning realises anti-duplicate guidance and is treated as functionally equivalent, so not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: maker r4: 'Search, tag filtering'; client r4: 'found it again by searching (even with different capitalization)'.
decisions.note: Conforming: search present and case-insensitive, affirmed by client.

decisions.evidence: maker r1/r4: 'tagging', 'tag filtering'; client r4: 'filtered by tag'.
decisions.note: Conforming: assign tags and filter by tag.

decisions.evidence: maker r2 behaviour list; client r2: 'adding links, opening them'.
decisions.note: Conforming: selecting an item opens the original url.

decisions.evidence: maker r4: 'four sort modes'; client r2: 'sorting'.
maker r4: 'Save links with manually entered titles, notes, and tags', 'Editing'; client r4: 'I saved a link with a title, notes, and tags'.
decisions.note: Conforming: save by url and edit bookmark fields.
